method.summary: How long does one keyless documentation call to this server take, from a caller that is nobody in particular? Fifteen calls to `query-docs`: five plain-language questions inside the scope the server's own tool description claims, each sent three times, in three rounds round-robin across eight of the nine solutions measured, so a slow minute on this container's network falls across all of them rather than on one. Median 1007.2 ms, min 835.7, max 1562.5, IQR 104.0; round medians 1014.6, 960.4, 1007.2 ms; 0 failures. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a server-side latency. Every number includes this container, its HTTP proxy and one day's public internet from a single vantage point; three rounds notice an outlier and cannot characterise a distribution over time. Response size is not controlled and is published beside every duration (median 2877 bytes of text here): a server returning more text is doing more work on the wire, which is a property of the corpus, not of its speed. NO BASELINE, deliberately: the job says 'within the agent's turn', which is not a number, and inventing one so the coverage table resolved to supports or contradicts would be filling a cell to make the map look finished. This record is a measurement; the adjudication is the reader's. NO RANKING and no comparison with the other records filed from this run: the question sets differ because the corpora differ. The protocol was pre-registered before any call was sent.
method.dataset: Five questions, each sent three times: How do I run cleanup code when a component is torn down?; How do I open a modal from a button?; How do I declare a model field the database computes?; Where do I register route middleware?; How do I build a model instance from a dict and validate it?
